extracted.intended_audience: professional mathematicians and advanced students of analytical geometry (readers of a 19th-century mathematical journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Propositions, definitions and formulae for analytical geometry referred to oblique coordinate axes (directing cosines, projecting coefficients, equations of straight lines, intersections, perpendiculars, loci, and related 3D geometry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonic mean relation in triangle-parabola construction
rubrics_metrics.description: CH is therefore an harmonic mean between AC and BC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived by showing BC:BC—CH :: EA:EC and AC:CH—AC :: EA:EC; alternative parabola-based derivations (bisect AB in E, use parabola properties DE(=EB):EB::EB:P implying P=EB and subsequent ratio manipulations) and Thibaut's solution using Hutton's proposition and algebraic manipulation to show CH = 2AC·CB/(AC+CB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic progression of cevians when squares of sides are arithmetic
rubrics_metrics.description: If the squares of the sides of a triangle be in arithmetical progression, the lines drawn from the angles to a point within the triangle so as to make equal angles with each other, are in arithmetical progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shown by writing squared side-lengths a^2,b^2,c^2 and squared cevians x^2,y^2,z^2, using the fact that equal mutual angles imply pairwise cosine(120°) terms, producing three equations (1),(2),(3) and subtracting to obtain linear relations that yield x,y,z in arithmetic progression. Special-case discussion: a second algebraic root is rejected unless the triangle is equilateral; in the equilateral case the alternative root corresponds to two lines and the third produced and yields the known chord-sum property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary on which cevian is arithmetic mean
rubrics_metrics.description: The line which is an arithmetical mean between the other two is the one drawn from the angle opposite that side whose square is a mean between the squares of the other two sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence of the previous theorem; indicates correspondence between side-square arithmetic means and corresponding cevian arithmetic means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locus of midpoints of equal chords in an ellipse (general equation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equation for the locus of the middle points of equal chords in an ellipse: derived algebraically in terms of chord half-lengths m,n and midpoint coordinates x,y, leading to an explicit quartic/quadratic relation (given in the solution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple solution methods provided. Behaviour descriptions: when a is small relative to b the locus is an oval similar to the ellipse; as c approaches b the locus becomes 'double knobbed' (double oval connected at origin); when c=b the locus is a double oval or lemniscate-like; when c > b and c ≫ a the locus splits into two equal open curves concave toward major axis. Special-case reduction: if a=b (circle) the equation reduces to a circle X^2 + Y^2 = a^2 - r^2 (radius (c^2 - a^2)^{1/2}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: angles of ordination and cosines of ordination
rubrics_metrics.description: The angles which the axes make with each other will be called the angles of ordination, and the cosines of these angles the cosines of ordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation: if f,g,h denote the cosines of the angles which axes of x & y, y & z, z & x make with each other, then f,g,h are the cosines of ordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: coefficient of cubature
rubrics_metrics.description: If F = [1 - f^2 - g^2 - h^2 + 2fgh]^{1/2} it will be termed the coefficient of cubature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in volume-related formulae when referring to oblique axes; several equivalent formulae given for r in terms of ordination angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition I — equations to a straight line (projecting coefficients)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (a,b,c) be a given point and (x,y,z) a variable point on the straight line; let r denote the distance between them. If l,m,n denote the constant ratios of the projections of r on the axes to r, then x - a : y - b : z - c = l r : m r : n r, i.e., x - a = l r, y - b = m r, z - c = n r are the equations to the straight line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines projecting coefficients l,m,n (projections of r on axes divided by r) and directing cosines (cosines of the angles the line makes with axes). Also notes that lr,mr,nr are the coordinate projections of r.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition II — equation of straight line through two points
rubrics_metrics.description: A straight line through points (x1,y1,z1) and (x2,y2,z2) can be represented in symmetric form (x - x1)/l = (y - y1)/m = (z - z1)/n where l,m,n are projecting coefficients; consistency with the second point yields ratios of differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the line passes through both points, (x2 - x1) : (y2 - y1) : (z2 - z1) = l : m : n, providing a method to determine l,m,n (up to a common factor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition III — condition for intersection of two straight lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two lines with equations expressed in projecting coefficients and base points, elimination leads to a determinant-like condition (equation (8)) that must vanish for the lines to intersect: (a - a')(m - m')(...)+... = 0 (full expression in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solve (7) for parameters r and r' and eliminate to obtain the explicit scalar condition (8). If condition holds, compute r or r' from (7) to get intersection coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition IV — distance between two given points via directing cosines
rubrics_metrics.description: The distance r between two given points equals the orthogonal projection sums: r = X_r(x2 - x1) + Y_r(y2 - y1) + Z_r(z2 - z1), where X_r,Y_r,Z_r are directing cosines of r; usual Euclidean distance r^2 = (Δx)^2 + (Δy)^2 + (Δz)^2 follows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method projects broken-line components on axes and on r to derive the standard distance formula and to express r by its directing cosines when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition V — relation among projecting coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Projecting coefficients l,m,n of a straight line satisfy l^2 + m^2 + n^2 + 2fmn + 2gln + 2hlm = 1, where f,g,h are cosines of ordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result obtained by eliminating coordinate differences and dividing by r^2 (equation (12)). This is the normalization relation linking projecting coefficients and the obliquity of axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition VI — find projecting coefficients from line equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Given symmetric line equations S : T : U, there is a scalar W satisfying Wl = S, Wm = T, Wn = U; and W = S^2 + T^2 + U^2 + 2(TU + SU + ST) (explicit formula (15) in text) determines W, then l,m,n = S/W, T/W, U/W.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an algebraic method to compute the projecting coefficients when the line is given in standard symmetric form; W is found from the relation (12) substituted with l,m,n = S/W etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition VII — directing cosines from projecting coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Directing cosines (X,Y,Z) of a line are given by X = (l + h m + g n)/√(...), with analogous cyclic formulae, and satisfy X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 = 1 (equations (16),(17)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute X,Y,Z by solving linear relations obtained by appropriate substitutions and normalizing; the denominator is the normalization factor (square root of the sum of squares plus mixed terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition VIII — projecting coefficients from directing cosines
rubrics_metrics.description: Given directing cosines X,Y,Z, the projecting coefficients l,m,n are determined by explicit formulae: l = [(1 - f^2)X + (f g - h)Y + (f h - g)Z]/Δ etc. (equations (18)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solve the linear system (16)-(17) for l,m,n in terms of X,Y,Z and the cosines of ordination; denominator factors depend on f,g,h and their combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition IX — relation among directing cosines
rubrics_metrics.description: The directing cosines X,Y,Z satisfy a quadratic relation obtained by combining (18) and (17); the explicit form is given as equation (19) in the text (a bilinear/quadratic relation linking X,Y,Z and the obliquity parameters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the counterpart of Proposition V in the space of directing cosines; used for consistency checks and to relate line direction to axis obliquity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition X — cosines that axes make with normals to coordinate planes
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulas for the cosines which the axes make with normals to the coordinate planes: substitute appropriate unit vectors into the directing-cosine relations to obtain p,q,r etc. as in equation (20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain by noting each normal is perpendicular to two axes and substituting special values into the general directing-cosine relation (19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition XI — angles (cosines) which a straight line makes with plane normals
rubrics_metrics.description: If r is a line with projecting coefficients l,m,n then the cosines A,M,N which r makes with the normals to the coordinate planes yz,xz,xy respectively are A = l r, M = m r, N = n r (equation (21)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are orthogonal projections of r on the normals; used when considering inclinations to coordinate planes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition XII — angle of inclination between two straight lines
rubrics_metrics.description: For lines with directing cosines X_i,Y_i,Z_i and X_j,Y_j,Z_j, cos φ = X_i X_j + Y_i Y_j + Z_i Z_j; alternative expressions in terms of projecting coefficients and obliquity parameters are given (equations (22)-(25)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides multiple equivalent formulae for the angle between lines: via directing cosines (dot product), via projecting coefficients with obliquity corrections, and expanded forms suitable for computation in oblique coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition XIII — conditions for perpendicularity of two lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Several equivalent conditions for two lines to be perpendicular: (i) Xi Xj + Yi Yj + Zi Zj = 0; (ii) relations among projecting coefficients (equation (32)); and expanded oblique-axis forms (equations (33)-(37)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the simplest dot-product condition in directing cosines when available; expanded forms are provided for working directly with projecting coefficients and cosines of ordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition XIV — condition for two straight lines to be parallel
rubrics_metrics.description: Two straight lines are parallel iff their projecting coefficients are proportional: l = l', m = m', n = n' (equations (38)-(40)), equivalently their directing cosines coincide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple proportionality test between symmetric forms or comparing directing cosines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition XV — length of perpendicular from a given point to a line
rubrics_metrics.description: Given point P(x1,y1,z1) and line with base point (a,b,c) and projecting coefficients l,m,n, the length r of the perpendicular from P to the line is determined by r = sqrt{[(x1 - a)^2 + (y1 - b)^2 + (z1 - c)^2] - [projection term]^2} with explicit projection formula (equations (41)-(45)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute orthogonal projection of broken-line components on the line to determine the perpendicular distance; coordinates of the foot are then a + l r, b + m r, c + n r (equation (43)). Special formulae for distances to coordinate axes given when origin substitutions are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition XVI — perpendicular distance between two skew lines
rubrics_metrics.description: For two non-coplanar (skew) lines, let t,m',n' be projecting coefficients and V be directing cosines of the common perpendicular; then relations X7 + f m + v n = 0, etc., lead to the formula for the shortest distance r' between the lines given by an expression (48) involving determinants of projecting coefficients and ordination cosines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the unique straight line perpendicular to both given lines (its directing cosines obtained via solving linear relations), then compute its length as orthogonal projection of the connecting broken line; detailed algebraic expression provided in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: projecting coefficients and directing cosines (terminology and interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projecting coefficients l,m,n are the constant ratios of the projections of the line-segment r on the axes to r. Directing cosines are the cosines of the directing angles (angles the line makes with the axes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projecting coefficients times r give coordinate differences between points on the line and a base point; directing cosines are normalized versions satisfying unit-length relations with obliquity corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of symmetric equations and introduced terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: The author employs symmetrical equations throughout and introduces new terms such as 'coefficient of cubature' and 'projecting coefficients' for quantities that constantly appear in oblique-axis inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advised approach: use symmetry for clarity; new terminology facilitates repeated formulae and manipulations relative to oblique axes.
